name: Mary Morgan

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mary Morgan was a Breton folkloric figure. This siren, or mermaid, was said to haunt the shores of Brittany, singing sweetly to draw sailors toward her dangerous rocks. She was especially linked to the Bay of Douarnenez, where the legendary princess Dahut was said to have built her crystal city of Ys. Sailors were warned to carry a crucifix or other amulet with them when they sailed past Mary Morgan's rocks.

okr.objective: Document Mary Morgan, the Breton siren who lured sailors to the rocks.
